key_insight: The model jointly generates video, replayable 3D motion for a supplied rig, and a camera that aligns the motion with the depicted scene. It bridges the gap between realistic motion in pixels and animation usable on a 3D asset.
problem_solved: Video generators can depict convincing actions but do not directly provide rig-specific 3D animation that can be replayed in a 3D scene.
method: Condition generation on a supplied rig—the skeletal structure used to animate a 3D asset.
Co-generate video and corresponding 3D motion rather than producing only pixels.
Generate a camera alongside the motion to align the 3D animation with the video.
impact: This approach could make generated actions usable in animation and 3D content workflows, beyond video-only outputs. The supplied abstract is truncated, so implementation details and performance results are not available.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: supplied rig → joint generation → video, 3D motion, and camera.
Side-by-side frames showing a monkey jumping over a crossbar in video and as a rigged 3D animation.
Camera-frustum diagram illustrating alignment between the animated asset and the video view.
Comparison panel: pixels-only output versus replayable 3D motion.
paper_title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
paper_authors: Noam Rotstein, Yoad Tewel, Chen Tessler, Haggai Maron, Gal Chechik
